A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from DiffuApriel to DiffuMamba. All 15 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, references, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and zero-shot evaluation results, throughput and latency measurements, and additional downstream results including MMLU in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original language-model evaluation results and reports expanded inference benchmarks and fitted latency analyses in Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: The retained backbones correspond to v1's +MLP variants, with the same diffusion objective. However, v3 Section 4.3 adds block-autoregressive inference that retains caches across blocks, propagates forward Mamba states across blocks, and restricts reverse scanning to the current block. v1 left block-diffusion integration to future work; this adaptation changes the inference procedure.

E1.justification: MMLU, evaluated in v1 Appendix A/Table 5, is absent from v3. DCLM training, seven held-out perplexity datasets, and the other five downstream tasks remain. Throughput scenarios expand to block-cached generation up to approximately 262K tokens, versus the earlier 65K maximum.

E2.justification: v1's efficiency comparison uses DiffuTran and Mamba variants. v3 Figure 2 adds evaluated DiffuTran + Fast-dLLM and hybrid + Fast-dLLM configurations, Transformer and Mamba autoregressive baselines, and comparisons among block-cached Transformer and Mamba models. These substantially broaden the actual comparator set.

E3.justification: v1 fixes 128 denoising steps; v3 uses K=L/p with p=8 or 16 and explicitly measures generated tokens divided by total decoding time. New protocols include 32-token blocks and longer generation ranges. Timing evaluation narrows from 0.5B/1.3B to the largest scale, warm-ups decrease from five to three, and Table 1 adds average perplexity across datasets.

E4.justification: v3 removes the with/without-MLP comparisons reported throughout v1. It adds comparisons of cache recomputation versus reuse and two denoising-step factors. Figure 3 introduces fitted quadratic, linear, and constant latency components at 1K and 65K tokens to investigate the source of scaling differences.

E5.justification: Reported timing averages change from 20 decoding runs in v1 Section 4.1 to five in v3. v3 also introduces constrained estimation of latency coefficients. Neither version reports confidence intervals, timing dispersion, training-seed variability, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained quality-table values exactly match v1's +MLP rows; v3 removes results without MLP layers and MMLU results, and adds average perplexities. Efficiency results are substantially replaced: Figure 2a reports 8.2×/4.3× gains at K=L/8, and Figure 2c reports 2.3×/1.9× over block-cached DiffuTran. These differ in conditions from v1's 4.4×/2.6× comparisons and do not establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The diffusion and backbone equations are largely retained or relocated. Beyond v1's brief backbone-complexity discussion, v3 Table 3 and Section 4.3 develop FLOP, memory-traffic, arithmetic-intensity, and throughput expressions covering AR and cached diffusion variants. Substituting K=L/p yields O(1/L²) versus O(1/L) throughput scaling for full-sequence Transformer and Mamba diffusion. This is a substantial analytical extension, without new theorem proofs.

C1.justification: The architectural feasibility contribution remains, but v3 makes systematic inference benchmarking and superiority over autoregressive baselines central contributions. Its abstract and conclusion identify cache-reusing Mamba block diffusion as the uniquely linear-scaling, highest-throughput strategy. v1 treated block diffusion as future work and centered its claims on backbone replacement and hybridization.

C2.justification: v3 explains declining full-sequence throughput when denoising steps grow with length, extending v1's fixed-step saturation account, and identifies cache reuse as crucial for beating AR inference. It more explicitly acknowledges small-scale generalization weaknesses. Appendix B adds substantive limitations concerning fixed acceptance factors, batch-one timing, and the absence of training optimized for cached block decoding.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix A/Table 6 newly discloses optimizer settings, learning-rate bounds and schedule, global batch size 512, weight decay, EMA, antithetic sampling, clipping, and additional Mamba implementation settings. These fill substantial reproducibility gaps. The earlier model-configuration table and conditioning equations are mostly relocated; the new disclosures do not establish changed training settings.

R1.justification: Most related work remains. v3 adds Caduceus, data-efficiency, and foundational attention references, explicitly acknowledges prior SSM diffusion for biological sequences, and credits related bidirectional backbones. Several reasoning-model and benchmark references disappear. These changes refine the literature coverage and text-specific novelty boundary without fundamentally replacing the research positioning.

P1.justification: Beyond model renaming and authorship updates, v3 substantially rewrites the introduction, contributions, and conclusion; places modeling quality before throughput; and moves detailed architectural mathematics into Appendix A. The earlier downstream appendix is replaced by configuration and limitations sections, with new takeaway summaries throughout the experimental narrative.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from one to two columns. Figure 2 is redesigned around decoding strategies and logarithmic throughput axes, replacing the earlier scale-specific throughput/latency panels. Figure 3 and complexity/hyperparameter tables are added. Quality tables remove variant rows, add an average column, and change placement; the configuration table moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the central efficiency argument through explicit total-decoding measurements, length-scaled steps, Fast-dLLM and AR controls, and analysis separating cache reuse from recomputation. Appendix A also fills major reproducibility gaps. These gains outweigh the removed MLP/MMLU evaluations and fewer timing repeats. Important qualifications remain: quality under the fastest cached decoding is unvalidated, and Section 4.3 incorrectly associates the 8.2×/4.3× ratios with K=L/16, whereas Figure 2 assigns them to K=L/8.
